# v6 FACTS ledger

**Method v4.1.** Every fact is computed under method v4.1: method v4 with canonical margins (scripts/naacl/router.py, MAPREFLECT_CANONICAL_MARGIN=1, margins rounded to 12 decimals and threshold ties routed) and the thresholds frozen on development in docs/naacl/results/v4_1_frozen.json, with unresolved stated-confidence answers treated as missing (V6_UQ_VALID_ONLY=1). Both fixes come from docs/naacl/v6/reviews/opendata_uq_audit/. Values that changed are kept as exploratory *PreFix facts where the plan asks for them. Generated by `scripts/naacl/v6_numbers.py`; do not edit by hand. Every number comes from the method-v4 frozen outputs or an offline analysis of them (no model call). Each fact `F-<ID>` is the macro `\F<ID>` in `paper/numbers_v6.tex` (with `\F<ID>Lo` and `\F<ID>Hi` when it has an interval). Status: confirmatory = one of v4's five pre-declared Holm contrasts; descriptive = v4, outside the Holm family; exploratory = computed after the v4 freeze (X1 to X6, and the stratified gates added after the freeze); note = a definition or method fact, no macro.

Intervals: 95% split-group bootstrap (scripts/naacl/group_stats.py, B = 2000, one shared draw). Signed values are points of accuracy unless the claim says otherwise.

## Reproduction of the v4 generators

The script reruns `v4_analysis.py`, `uq_ablation.py` (v4 mode) and `newdata_analysis.py` in memory with every write intercepted (none reaches paper/), and compares each regenerated file with its committed copy; pre-v6 paper files are compared with their archived copies in paper_archive/pre_v6_2026-10-10/:
Two checks. (1) The v4 path, unchanged: the script reruns `v4_analysis.py`, `uq_ablation.py` (v4 mode) and `newdata_analysis.py` without canonical margins in a separate process, every write intercepted, and compares each regenerated file with its committed copy (pre-v6 paper files with paper_archive/pre_v6_2026-10-10/):

| F-IntDefinitions | X1 definitions | Outcomes rejoined by full field identity (the v4 key) to results/naacl/v2/reflect/given (doubt = 'naive', Self-Refine, neutral A, neutral+check AC, neutral+evidence B, reflect BC) and to the v4 rows (widen action, routed action) and fresh_<W>_runs; a row is dropped, not filled, when the stored first pass differs. Fresh mapping is measured only where the widened pool adds candidates (its runner skipped the rest), so its row covers those pairs. Scorer: target_correct, ITOpsGraph v2.1. The 30% is chosen within each model over that population, ties sharing the boundary; random is the exact expectation on the same population. Calls and tokens: v2 arm token logs (results/naacl/v2/tokens) per reflected field, check calls included; v4 actions as in v4_analysis.cost(). |  |  |  | note |

| F-CalDefinitions | X4 definitions | Answered (valid) first passes, all test fields per model. Reliability: 10 equal-width top-score bins, 1.0 in the last; ECE = sum over bins of (bin share) x |accuracy - mean top score|; Brier = mean (top score - correct)^2. Margin deciles keep ties together (a tied value goes to the decile of its first sorted position), so deciles can be empty or uneven. AUROC: errors positive, low margin = error, split-group bootstrap interval. These margin AUROCs are on every answered field, not the uq population of Table 3. |  |  |  | note |

| F-RouterErrDefinition | X2 error trigger (map_reflect/map_reflect_runner.py, detect_mapping_errors and the trigger loop) | A field fires when the runner's detect_mapping_errors returned any message. The checks: the ranking cannot be parsed (declined); the top prediction is prefixed by the source product; a source field ending in _id names another table the prediction lacks; high name overlap with a reason citing name similarity; type keywords (string, int, date, ...) disagree; top score below 0.6; top two scores within 0.1. The runner stored this list with every v2 first pass (predictions[field].detected_errors), so the trigger is read, not re-derived. It is binary: at Map-Reflect's per-model share, fired fields are routed first (an equal fraction of each when they exceed the budget) and any remaining budget is spread evenly over the others (exact expectation). |  |  |  | note |
| F-RouterNbrDefinition | X2 neighbourhood trigger | The runner's 'neighborhood' trigger is not sibling disagreement: it fires when neighbor_k > 0 and the top two scores of the runner-order initial ranking differ by less than 0.2 (a TODO placeholder in the code). It is therefore a fixed-threshold margin, reported only for completeness. Sibling disagreement on the target type or table is vacuous here, because every candidate a field sees belongs to the one named target type, so all siblings agree on type and table by construction; that router is dropped. |  |  |  | note |

| F-PDRetrievalDefinitions | Table 1 model-free columns, definitions | No LLM. Same fields, named target type and scorer as Table 1 (Granite-4 v4 test rows define the population only; core: test minus old development; held-out: test manifests; eval.calc_accuracy.target_correct; ITOpsGraph v2.1 labels). Candidates: the named target type's fields (data/v4_pools shown + type_rest, minus the source field). Input text per field, the standard input of the hybrid retriever: field name with its parent type (the catalogue id, which carries product, type and field) plus the catalogue description, as '<id>: <description>'; the query is the source field's id and description the same way (id alone when the catalogue has no entry, Valentine and NL2GQL sources). BM25: rank_bm25 BM25Okapi, the runner's field-name tokenizer with each token further split on non-alphanumerics, document frequencies over the whole catalogue. Dense: cosine with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, the encoder of the hybrid order, local CPU. Hybrid: first entry of the hybrid20 order (dense + BM25 over the catalogue, reciprocal rank fusion k=60, then the named type's fields), recomputed by the same fusion where v4_pools.py had left stored order (F-PDHybridRecomputed). Ties break by a fixed hash of the candidate id, never by stored or retrieval order. Cupid and Similarity Flooding: valentine 1.0.0 defaults (Cupid with acceptance threshold 0 so every pair is scored), schema only with no instances, so they see field names (all-capitals names lower-cased) and parent-type table names but not descriptions (on Bio-ML, whose field names are bare OMIM and Orphanet numbers, the column name is the class label, as AnyTool's adaptation); per sample the scored source fields against the union of their named-type candidates, top-1 per source field within its own candidates, a field with no scored pair counts as wrong. Average: unweighted mean over datasets. |  |  |  | note |

| F-PDDefinitions | Table 1 definitions | Field accuracy (%) on the v4 test fields of each core dataset (test minus old development), named target type, full-identity scorer, ITOpsGraph v2.1, backbone Granite-4-H-small for every LLM column. MatchMaker: the protocol v2 run (results/naacl/v2_baselines/bases/*__matchmaker-granite; Valentine with the expected_target fallback). Magneto: released code, zero-shot bipartite reranking with descriptions (desc-bp), no LLM. Prompt-Matcher: the protocol v2 Granite-4 run on the same first pass. AnyTool: the faithful implementation (anytool/anytool_faithful.py, scripts/naacl/v6_calls/anytool_t1.py), target given, on Granite-4. Stated adaptations: (1) the expected_target fallback, when the utterance or AnyTool's product parse yields no target (Valentine, OMOP), MatchMaker and AnyTool use the record's named target; (2) on ToolBench, AnyTool's solver lists the named target tool's fields first, so its 100-candidate cap cannot drop them (the run with the original order is F-PDAnyToolToolBenchCapped); (3) on the five held-out sets, AnyTool and MatchMaker see exactly the target candidates each record lists, the list Map-Reflect and Magneto see; on Bio-ML, whose source classes are bare OMIM numbers, AnyTool's solver sees each source as its id with its label. AnyTool answers are translated from its hierarchy names back to lookup ids. Prompt-Matcher on the held-out sets: its answer accuracy Pr comes from the pooled development fit of the ten core sets (SemTab and SchemaNet have no development split and MIMIC-OMOP's is thin), the transfer setting of Map-Reflect's thresholds, which are frozen from core development. A field a baseline did not answer counts as wrong. Average: unweighted mean over the ten datasets, printed only when the column is complete. |  |  |  | note |

| F-PDGptOssDefinitions | Table 1 gpt-oss-120b block definitions | The Granite-4 block's definitions (F-PDDefinitions) and every stated adaptation carry over unchanged: the expected_target fallback, MatchMaker's named target type, the target-first candidate order for AnyTool on ToolBench, the held-out listed candidates for AnyTool and MatchMaker, Bio-ML sources shown to AnyTool with their labels, and Prompt-Matcher's pooled core-development fit (here from gpt-oss's own core calibration). Backbone gpt-oss-120b on ENDPOINT_A (gpt-oss-120b-a100). ToolBench is scored on the fixed-seed 400-sample draw (docs/naacl/results/t1_gptoss_toolbench_draw.json) in every column of this block. Prompt-Matcher runs one arm, pm30, the arm closest to the method's frozen development routed share for gpt-oss (19.3%), under the field-first description treatment (ff1) where a set has an ff1 lookup. AnyTool and MatchMaker keep their own description cuts (80 and 100 characters), as in their published designs. Further adaptation: MatchMaker on Bio-ML and Val. OpenData ran as 5 and 4 parallel shards of the sorted test population (docs/naacl/results/t1_gptoss_mm_shards.json, fixed before any shard call) because the endpoint slowed and a MatchMaker run writes nothing until it ends; each shard ran its own one-pass self-improvement (9 passes instead of 2), and each merged run holds exactly the set's population. Magneto-BP calls no model; its Granite-4-block predictions are rescored on this block's populations. |  |  |  | note |

| F-MMAuditFindings | MatchMaker OMOP audit (Codex review C2) | OMOP-CMS: correct 48, abstained 13, wrong, gold not among its candidates 12, wrong, gold among its candidates 12 of 85; 3 parse warnings; 1.48 candidates per field, 84 fields with no semantic-index candidate; OMOP-MIMIC: correct 38, wrong, gold not among its candidates 27, abstained 8, wrong, gold among its candidates 5, abstained, top candidate correct 3 of 78; 1 parse warnings; 2.17 candidates per field, 70 fields with no semantic-index candidate; OMOP-Synthea: correct 55, wrong, gold not among its candidates 6, abstained 3, abstained, top candidate correct 2, wrong, gold among its candidates 1 of 65; 3 parse warnings; 1.92 candidates per field, 58 fields with no semantic-index candidate. Earlier Llama-3.3 run (before the fix): OMOP-CMS 44 of 60 answered fields outside the named table; OMOP-MIMIC 38 of 61 answered fields outside the named table; OMOP-Synthea 47 of 65 answered fields outside the named table. Scorer: full identity (target_correct), the same v4 test fields as Table 1. Table 1's MatchMaker cells use the reflection base (reflect_on_baseline.prepare_matchmaker), which keeps the top candidate of an abstained field as its answer; correct plus 'abstained, top candidate correct' reproduces each Table 1 cell, and F-MMAudit*OwnAcc gives the accuracy with abstentions counted as no answer. Why the semantic step is silent: match_maker_agent._semantic_candidate_generation asks the index (the whole OMOP catalogue: source and target tables) for top_k + |source fields| + 10 neighbours and then keeps only fields of the named target table, so on OMOP almost no neighbour survives and MatchMaker chooses among its LLM reasoning candidates alone. No field selects outside the named table after the type-hint fix (commit 9663e8a); before it most did. Parse warnings are few and per call. Fixing the semantic window would need a rerun. |  |  |  | note |

| F-FeatAblProvenance | the feature ablation | From the Codex review of code 3926722 (docs/naacl/v6/reviews/review_3926722/feature_ablation.py and .json). Exploratory: specified after the test results were seen; intervals are paired split-group bootstraps, unadjusted. Each variant refits the benefit model on development only, with the same grouped cross-validation for C and the same threshold rule, and is scored on the same stored test reflections at matched calls per field (frozen development cost estimates, whole-field stopping). The full-feature refit reproduces the frozen model's C, threshold and accuracy, and the development cost correction leaves the threshold unchanged. Rerun here: every value identical. Each variant selects C by grouped dev CV log loss and threshold by cross-fitted dev net repairs, same as v5. Test intervention fixed; matched cost uses frozen dev cost estimates and whole-field observed-spend stopping. Same full-dev scaling as original fitting code. |  |  |  | note |

| F-SampleKDefinitions | U7 definitions | Answer entropy from the first k of the five stored draws per field (results/naacl/v6/u9/samples), k = 1 to 5, for Granite-4 and Llama-4 only; gpt-oss and Qwen3.5 stored only the five-draw entropy, so they are not in U7. Draws are clustered by answer identity, a declined or unreadable draw being its own cluster, as uq_baselines_v3 scores answer entropy; the five-draw value reproduces the stored one (F-SampleKMismatch). AUROC on within-model ranks with the UQ run's split-group bootstrap; the routing swap uses v4's routed share and second pass. With k = 1 every field has entropy 0: its routing is the random gate's (ties share the budget), and its AUROC differs from 0.5 only because ranks are pooled within each model. |  |  |  | note |

| F-VFiveStratInputs | reflection strategies on v5: each dataset's arm inputs (the same for all four models) | NL2GQL, Val. ChEMBL, Val. OpenData, Val. TPC-DI, Val. WikiData: v5 inputs (task 1b rerun); ITOpsGraph: v5 inputs (task 1b rerun, 274 of 377 scored fields; the rest byte-identical prompts); OMOP-CMS, OMOP-MIMIC, OMOP-Synthea: v5 prompts (R-X1 ff1 rerun); ToolBench: v5 prompts (stored rows, byte-identical) |  |  |  | note |
| F-VFiveStratDefinitions | reflection strategies on v5: definitions | Each strategy's answer replaces the first answer on the fields it is applied to. Doubt, Self-Refine and the four neutral arms (neutral reflection, with the pairwise check, with symmetric evidence, with both) reflect over the first ranking's candidates. Widen + reflect is v5's second pass with widening (neutral reflection with symmetric evidence and the either-order check over the widened pool) on every field. Reflect or widen + reflect is v5's second pass with the action its rule names per field. Selections: every field; v5's own selection (u(x) above its frozen tau, 32.0% of fields); and a random selection of the same share in each cell (in expectation). Gains against the first pass on the v5 test fields, pooled over field-model pairs, split-group bootstrap (B = 2,000). Arm outcomes read with the protocol v2 parser except the rerun cells (v5's parser). |  |  |  | note |
| F-BudgetDefinitions | U1 definitions | Uq population (answered core-test fields with every signal of their model, uq_ablation_v4.run's own population and v4 second pass). Each signal routes its least confident share b of every model's fields, b = 0 to 100% in steps of 5, ties sharing the boundary (uq_ablation.gate_weights); random is the exact expectation; the oracle routes the fields the action repairs first. Signals on fewer models are curved on those models, with the margin's curve on the same models beside them. Reach: smallest b whose change is at least 95% of the every-field change. |  |  |  | note |
| F-DetDefinitions | U2 definitions | AUROC, AUPRC (errors positive) and AURC (risk-coverage, most confident first) on within-model percentile ranks pooled over the models that have the signal; AUROC interval from the UQ run's own split-group bootstrap draws. ECE (10 equal-width bins) and Brier after an isotonic map fitted per model on the old development fields (manifest old_dev_excluded: the only development fields that carry the paid signals). The token log-probability has no development outputs and the logistic is cross-fitted on test, so neither is calibrated. Held-out pooled AUROC: the 20 held-out cells of uq_ablation_v4.heldout_aurocs, ranks within model. |  |  |  | note |
| F-MVarDefinitions | U3 definitions | From the first pass's sorted score list: raw margin s1 - s2; normalised margin (s1 - s2) / sum of the non-negative scores; ratio log((s1 + 0.001) / (s2 + 0.001)); score entropy (negated, normalised); top-1 minus top-3 gap s1 - s3. Routing at v4's share with the v4 second pass, uq population. |  |  |  | note |
| F-RPartDefinitions | U4 definitions | Thresholds refit on the v4 development split (results/naacl/v4/dev/given, full identity, ITOpsGraph v2.1; reproduces the frozen development accuracy exactly) with each model's frozen widen action and the check, then applied to test. Margin only: no near-tie band, every routed field widens, t_m refit on v4_fit's quantile grid. Top score only: a field is routed when declined or its top score is at most t, t refit on the top-score quantile grid. Shared: one t_m on the 0.05 grid for all models (pooled development accuracy, ties to fewer calls). Development size: t_m and t_s refit per model on v4_fit's grids using a random 10, 25 or 50% of the development samples (50 draws each); 100% reproduces the frozen thresholds. |  |  |  | note |
| F-CovDefinitions | U5 definitions | Struct sends declined fields and fields of a named type wider than the 20 shown candidates to the frozen widen action; margin is Map-Reflect; union and intersection combine the two field sets (the union's struct-only fields widen); the logistic predicts a first-pass error from the struct flag, the declined flag and the margin, cross-fitted per model over split groups (2 folds x 5 repeats), and routes Map-Reflect's per-model share. Costs from the v4 token logs as Table 1. |  |  |  | note |
| F-AcceptDefinitions | U6 definitions | Map-Reflect's routing and per-field action; only the acceptance of the reflection's proposal (field_proposed) changes. No check: take the proposal. Check: the stored v4 answer. Own margin: take a changed proposal only when the reflection's revised margin exceeds the first-pass margin (v4_fit's 'check+margin' criterion, without the check). Both: the check and the margin rule. Near-tie proposals store no revised margin, so there the last two rules use the check. A check call follows a changed answer. |  |  |  | note |
| F-LogpDefinitions | U8 definitions | Stored per field by uq_baselines_v3 (per-token values were not kept): lp_answer and lp_answer_min are the sum and minimum log-probability of the tokens spelling the first ranked candidate's id (candidate tokens only); lp_mean and lp_entropy are the mean token log-probability and mean top-5 entropy over every token up to the end of that candidate (scores, formatting and any preamble included). So the candidate-only signal an earlier review asked for is the paper's lp_answer; U8 compares it with the all-token versions. |  |  |  | note |
| F-SemEntSeeds | answer entropy: sampling seeds | The endpoint_b client sends a fixed RANDOM_SEED (42) with sampling decoding, so five draws of one prompt come back identical. We gave each draw its own seed (42 to 46) at temperature 0.7, which makes them five independent draws, as the ENDPOINT_A draws for gpt-oss and Qwen3.5 are. |  |  |  | note |
| F-MCalDefinitions | U10 definitions | Isotonic maps fitted per model on the answered v4 development fields (margin, and the top score for comparison), applied to the answered test fields. Raw margin taken as a probability as is (it lies in [0, 1]). ECE with 10 equal-width bins; Brier = mean squared error. |  |  |  | note |
| F-NeedsRuns | items that need model calls (phase 2) |  |  |  |  | note |
